title: EO Pass Planner: browser-based prediction of Earth-observation satellite passes over a region of interest
description:
Static, client-side web application that predicts when Earth-observation instruments image a point or polygon region of interest. Orbital elements (CelesTrak) are propagated with SGP4, and each instrument swath is intersected with the region in a local equal-area projection. Swath models cover nadir-symmetric imagers, side-looking SAR, tasked sensors (field of regard), lidar and altimeter profiles and geostationary view geometry, for a catalogue of 74 optical, hyperspectral, thermal, SAR, lidar, meteorological, atmospheric and geophysics missions.

For each pass it reports time (UTC and local), region coverage, viewing and illumination geometry, orbit direction, expected cloud and atmospheric conditions, and whether the acquisition is systematic or a tasking opportunity. Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 passes are cross-checked against ESA acquisition plans, and past passes against real acquisitions in STAC catalogues. Results export as CSV, iCalendar, GeoJSON and GeoLibre projects.

The engine agrees with the reference implementation (eo-overpass-predictor) to within 0.06 s and 0.1 percentage points of coverage, and predicted times agree with 330 Sentinel-2 and Landsat scenes to about 1 s with element sets less than a week old. The archive contains the application and the orbital data at the time of release; the live application updates its data every 6 h.
